linkedin.activityText: Katie Couric Katie Couric 2mo Katie Couric shared this An hour of being serious and silly at the same time, which I've spent a whole career being told you're not supposed to do. Thank you Connor Diemand-Yauman ! Connor Diemand-Yauman Connor Diemand-Yauman 2mo Katie Couric shared this For years, Katie Couric struggled with which identity to bring to work. "People often aren't allowed in a professional setting to be multi-dimensional," she told me during our latest episode of Is This Working?! (out today). "You're put in a box, and people have a hard time if they can't categorize you." I've been thinking about that ever since. Identity and work is such a rich, perplexing topic--and not just for America's sweetheart. On the one hand, we're programmed to be excellent at work. To find that Goldilocks zone of kind but firm, humble but decisive, serious but lighthearted ("but never too silly..." a mentor once told me). On the other, we're told that work should be the fullest, most authentic expression of who we are. Like our job is the Rorschach test of our soul (no pressure!). But what I realized after this interview was that the very tension that Katie Couric struggled with for years--Katherine or Katie, serious journalist or smiley cutup--is exactly what made her irreplaceable. Nobody else could grill a sitting president at 7:05, then fly across Rockefeller Plaza dressed as Peter Pan flinging confetti at 8:43. Which makes me wonder: how many of us are sanding off our messy contradictions at work in service of picking a lane? In this conversation, Katie and I go deep on this topic and lots more. I couldn't believe how unfiltered she was: how fame fucked with her head, what she's still thin-skinned about, what her late husband Jay told her at the end of his life about what really matters. Plus pickleball, breast milk, and a report card grading my interview chops. If you filed Katie Couric under "Serious Important Newswoman" and never got to see her be heartbroken and hilarious in the same beat, I think you'll really like this one. Watch the full episode here: https://lnkd.in/gwiBYy3b . And I'm genuinely curious: how have you thought about balancing (or not) your many identities at work and life? posts.caption: The Cornell case has unleashed a torrent of first-person accounts from women revisiting traumatic experiences they had long kept buried. Here are just a few of them.

In the never admit you’ve made a mistake department, @tmztv caught up with Sen. Eric Schmitt after #JackSmith hearing on Tuesday to ask about the Atlanta Hawks–Iowa Hawkeyes basketball game mix-up. Watch what the senator had to say about the exchange. 👀

#Repost @tmztv

This was truly unbelievable.  In a much-talked-about exchange during Tuesday’s hearing, Sen. Eric Schmitt accused former special counsel Jack Smith of attending an Atlanta Hawks NBA basketball game on February 3, 2024. It appears Sen. Schmitt was attempting to show that Smith had perjured himself and was involved in a plot with Atlanta prosecutors to take down Trump. (FYI: Around this time, Atlanta prosecutor Fani Willis was leading a criminal investigation into Trump that was mired in drama and was eventually dropped last fall.)

During the hearing, Sen. Schmitt showed a poster board, held up by Louisiana Sen. John Kennedy (who, during the hearing, said that Smith made him want to “throw up in my mouth”), displaying text messages among Smith’s team about a basketball game. A different basketball game. Schmitt and his staff had mixed up the Atlanta Hawks with the IOWA Hawkeyes….a women's basketball game Smith had attended when they played at the University of Maryland.

When Smith denied attending the Atlanta Hawks game in February, Sen. Schmitt called Smith a “dirtbag” and said, “I think you’ve already perjured yourself.”

Sen. Amy Klobuchar invited Smith to respond to Schmitt’s accusation, at which point he clarified that he was at a women’s NCAA basketball game in Maryland that night, not Atlanta. Sen. Klobuchar suggested that Schmitt had confused the Atlanta Hawks with the Iowa Hawkeyes. After the hearing, Klobuchar posted on X: “Before calling someone a ‘dirtbag,’ the Senator should have had his facts straight. An apology is in order.”
But wait! There’s more: Senator Eric Schmitt is being mentioned as a possible JD Vance running mate for 2028. Axios reported that Schmitt has grown close to Vance and is viewed as a “top prospect.” Its sources say Vance considers him trustworthy, intelligent and politically skilled. 😳

📹: CSPAN

Happy Pub Day! Thank you Danny! ❤️❤️❤️ PS. My assistant Alyssa who produced this interview and I celebrated where else but @shakeshack !!!!! 🍔🥤😋

Bread of Angels is now out in paperback. You can watch our full conversation on my YouTube channel (link in bio) or listen wherever you get your podcasts.

This is one of the most consequential elections of my lifetime. So consider this a reminder friends! 

If you want to make sure your vote counts this year, make a plan now:

1. Go to Vote.gov⁠￼, choose your state, and check your registration—even if you’ve voted before. Update it if you’ve moved or changed your name.

2. Check your state’s deadlines and decide whether you’ll vote early, by mail, or in person on Election Day.

3. Look up your polling place, hours, and any ID requirements before you go.

4. Put your voting plan on your calendar. If voting by mail, request and return your ballot early.

Questions or trouble voting? Call or text the nonpartisan Election Protection hotline: 866-OUR-VOTE (866-687-8683).

 “Someone struggled for your right to vote. Use it.”
—Susan B. Anthony (historical rock star and badass) 

“Every election is determined by the people who show up.”
—-Larry Sabato (my friend and founder and director of the Center for Politics at @uva)

Earlier this week, Paramount Skydance reached a settlement with California Attorney General Rob Bonta and 11 other states that had sued to block its proposed $110 billion merger with Warner Bros. Discovery, clearing a major hurdle for the deal.

The merger would bring together two historic film studios, Paramount and Warner Bros.; two popular streaming platforms, Paramount+ and HBO Max; and two news organizations, CBS News and CNN, under the leadership of David Ellison.

While Bonta praised the terms of the settlement, he made clear that it did not mean he supported the merger, saying, “This settlement is not a vote of support for this merger.”

As part of the agreement, the combined company will be required to release at least 30 films a year for the first two years and 32 films a year for the following three years, with financial penalties if it falls short. Paramount also agreed to invest more than $1 billion in U.S. production and film releases and establish independent editorial boards overseeing CNN and CBS News.

When I spoke with Marc Elias (@democracydocket) on my podcast, I asked him about the merger and what it could mean for CNN and the broader media landscape. Marc has been outspoken about his concerns, telling me that if Ellison takes control of CNN, he believes it would be “incredibly dangerous” and “damaging to democracy.”

Watch our full conversation at the link in my bio.

Trump escalated his war with the media by blocking CNN from joining him on Air Force One as he travels to Knoxville, Tennessee  on Saturday to attend a college football game, a CNN spokeswoman confirmed. According to @npr, CNN was replaced by the conservative network Real America’s Voice News.

The news comes just after Trump’s ban on CNN, MS NOW, and Politico journalists lifted and network pool coverage was up and running again. CNN’s spot on Air Force One was reserved for a member of the U.S. network video pool, which Real America’s Voice News is not part of. 

This is a developing story.

📷: Getty/Johnny Louis

“Genuine emergency.”

That’s how @scaramucci describes the current moment in Washington, arguing that the administration is testing the limits of presidential power and the institutions meant to check it.

In this conversation, the Mooch and I discuss the role of the courts, the administration’s approach to power and conflict, and what it could all mean heading into the midterms.

Watch the full conversation on YouTube (link in bio) or listen wherever you get your podcasts.

The major TV networks–CNN, Fox News, ABC, CBS, and NBC– will resume their pool coverage of Trump on Friday, after they received confirmation from the Trump administration that CNN would be allowed back into the pool rotation. On Thursday evening, the White House denied CNN and MS NOW journalists from covering the arrival of Chinese leader Xi Jinping to the White House for a state dinner. @cnn reported that other television networks were allowed to cover the event. The White House allowed CNN to send a photo journalist and audio technician to the event, but not a reporter and producer who tried to gain access.

Xi Jinping's visit to the White House hasn’t been covered on major American networks so far. On Truth Social, Trump posted that the networks had “refused” to cover the event, not mentioning that outlets were barred from the grounds. On Thursday morning, despite having their press access restored overnight by a federal judge, some reporters from CNN, Politico, and MS NOW were still denied access to the White House. Their credentials have been restored as of Thursday afternoon. 

📷: AP Photo/Alex Brandon

What happens when the lawyers who once “flooded the zone” to defend civil rights and democracy start sitting on the sidelines?

@democracydocket founder Marc Elias says the retreat of some of the country’s biggest law firms is changing the legal landscape and making it harder for nonprofits and smaller firms to take on cases across the country.

We talked about what he believes is behind this shift, how it’s affecting the legal battles being fought right now, and what it could mean for the future of our legal system.

Watch the full conversation on YouTube (link in bio) or listen wherever you get your podcasts.
